diagram_math_checks.justification: Vertices a,b,c are labeled s1,s2,s3. def-cg-coxeter-nerve-and-moussong-metric clauses (1)-(2) identify cells with positive-definite principal submatrices. For each pair, C_T=[[1,-1/2],[-1/2,1]] has minors 1 and 3/4, so all three edges exist, as computed in Verification 1.1. Explicit segments a-b, b-c, c-a show exactly three unoriented edges; each vertex has degree two. No extra edge or arrow is asserted.

The nerve definition gives edge length arccos(-cos(π/m))=π-π/m. At m=3 this is 2π/3, justifying each edge label and matching Example (i), Fact F1 and Verification 1.1. Straight planar coordinates encode incidence only; the caption explicitly disclaims spherical-angle and planar-isometric interpretation.

C_S=(3/2)I-(1/2)J annihilates (1,1,1), hence is not positive definite. By the nerve definition (1)-(3), S is not a simplex. The drawing fills only three vertex dots, never its interior, and labels the interior no 2-simplex, matching Verification 2.1 and the metric-flag definition (3).
The three edge cells form precisely a 3-cycle with no 2-cell. Summing 3*(2π/3)=2π gives the displayed perimeter and agrees with Verification 3.1. No planar angle or area is labeled.
Original Verification steps 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 are byte-unchanged. They establish the claims without referring to the added picture, which is placed after Verification in final Remarks.
